subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity fit for Finsolve
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity fit for Finsolve

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side so we all have the same playbook. Please reply with any corrections.

TL;DR: Finsolve looks like a solid fit for Redwood Dedicated if your goals around predictable throughput and data isolation are firm. Next steps: technical deep-dive w/ David, sizing proposal & MAP, procurement intro for contract timeline.

What we heard (pain points)
- Variability in latency under peak (spikes > 300ms p95) during morning batch runs impacting customer SLAs
- Costs are unpredictable with on-demand GPUS; need predictable unit economics for forecasts
- Security/compliance needs: customer data must be isolated and retained per your retention policy; audit logs required

Current stack
- Inference runs on a mix of on-prem A100s + burst to cloud for peak; model: in-house T5-XXL variant
- Request pattern: steady baseline ~350 TPS during business hours, spikes up to ~800 TPS for short bursts (10-20 min), many short requests (avg seq len ~120 tokens)

Success criteria (what would make Dedicated a go)
- Predictable p95 latency <= 120ms for production traffic
- Committed baseline capacity to cover 400-500 TPS with burst to 800 TPS without significant degradation
- Dedicated GPU pools for data isolation and compliance; KMS integration for key management

Dedicated fit notes (what we'd propose)
- Reserved GPU pool sized for baseline 500 TPS with autoscaling policy for burst headroom to 900 TPS (burst via pre-warmed nodes and ephemeral capacity)
- Quantization recommendations to hit latency targets without quality regressions; we’ll run evals against your prompt set
- Isolation: tenancy model with customer-owned VPC & HSM/KMS support for keys

Open Qs from today
- Exact duration/frequency of the 800 TPS spikes (sustained vs short) — helps sizing and autoscale policy
- Procurement timeline and any required legal terms (SOC2 attestation; SLA targets)

Next steps
1) I’ll attach a draft sizing + pricing spreadsheet and our Dedicated one-pager — please review (attached).
2) David — can you lead a 60-min technical deep-dive next week (M/W/F slots) to validate sizing and integration points?
3) Alex — please introduce procurement contact so we can align on contracting timeline; Rafael will surface indicative commercial terms.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-onepager.pdf, redwood-dedicated-pricing-20260520.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — that summary captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Spikes to ~800 TPS are typically short-lived (10-25 minutes) but happen multiple times during heavy reporting windows (around 9-11am ET). Baseline is closer to 300-400 TPS.
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms would be acceptable, but the tighter the better.
- Security: we do require tenant isolation and audit logs for all inference requests tied to customer IDs. KMS is a must.

Procurement: looping in our procurement lead, Christine Miller (procurement@finsolve.com), who will handle contract flow and terms. Our timeline: target production in Q3; procurement kickoff in early June.

Please include an estimate for committed baseline + burst pricing and any SLAs you can offer. Happy to schedule the technical deep-dive — Wed 26 May or Fri 28 May afternoons ET work for us.

— Alex
